dependencies.basis: MINTED 2026-09-06 (round 4 re-open pass) from the IMF's own e-GDDS Important Dates table — the page headed 'Enhanced General Data Dissemination System / Important Dates', whose three columns are 'Participant', 'Date Metadata First Posted on the DSBB' and 'Date e-GDDS NSDP First Posted'. The page is at https://dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/important-dates-history and is client-rendered; the row is served by the endpoint cited, read direct with a plain browser-UA curl 2026-09-06. A non-null ComplianceDate in that row IS the e-GDDS NSDP first-posted date, which is what makes this a participation record rather than a list membership. Cross-checked against api/country/getcountrybytype?countryType=EGDDS (110 participants) — and the same list carries every country the corpus already wires to imf-e-gdds at A, so these stand on the same footing as ten existing edges. GRADED B, NOT A, DELIBERATELY: the endpoint's payload does not itself spell out 'Enhanced General Data Dissemination System' — the artefact is named by the page that consumes it and by the request. A Chrome read of https://dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/important-dates-history, where the heading and the country row are on one rendered page, would clear the A bar under the 2026-09-04 direct-read ruling; that is the one cheap upgrade left on all three of these. REOPENS a 2026-08 `unreadable-source` refusal. That round found the IMF press release 'Tajikistan Implements the International Monetary Fund's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System' (March 2020, pr20/96) by search but could not fetch its body text, and recorded the edge as real-but-unquotable. The date table gives the same fact as a first-party record: NSDP first posted 2020-03-17, which is that press release's month.

_dropped.why: THE ORIGINAL REFUSAL WAS RIGHT, AND NOW FOR A DOCUMENTED REASON 2026-09-06. `ly-cpi-social-protection.json` recorded that dsbb.imf.org 'returned only navigation shell content to every fetch attempt' — a claim about the fetcher, and the site reads fine through the API. Read properly, it confirms the refusal rather than overturning it. Libya IS on the e-GDDS participating list (110 countries), but its Important Dates row is {"CountryDisplayName":"Libya","CountryName":null,"CountryCode":null,"ObsFlag":false,"SubscriptionDate":null,"DSBBPostedDate":"2009-12-07T00:00:00","ComplianceDate":null,"ExternalDebtDate":null} — metadata posted to the DSBB in December 2009, which is GDDS-era, and **ComplianceDate null, meaning no e-GDDS NSDP has ever been posted**. The three countries in this pass with a null ComplianceDate (Libya, Lebanon, Haiti) are exactly the three whose edges stay refused, and the three with a date are exactly the three minted. Libya's separate SDDS/SDDS Plus refusal also stands: LBY appears in neither list (49 and 32 countries respectively).

SWEEP STATUS 2026-09-06. The eight dsbb.imf.org write-offs named in `notes/imf-dsbb-2026-09-06.md` were all read through the API this round and all eight are now settled: three minted (Tajikistan, Vanuatu, Honduras), three confirmed refused with a documented reason (Libya, Lebanon, Haiti — null ComplianceDate), two confirmed as already correct (Gabon denied on SDDS/SDDS Plus, Guatemala already live via gt-ine). **The class is closed for these eight, but not for the corpus**: `api/country/getcountrybytype` and `api/country/getsubscriptiondateInfos` between them give the definitive membership and implementation date of all three tiers for every country, and no round has ever swept the corpus's e-GDDS/SDDS edges against them. That sweep would check every one of the ~50 existing `-> imf-e-gdds` and ~30 `-> imf-sdds` edges in one pass, and would catch any that are wrong in the other direction.
